name: RuO2 altermagnetism
claim: RuO2 is a room-temperature collinear antiferromagnet / d-wave altermagnet with spin-split bands and a crystal (anomalous) Hall effect. Counter-claim: bulk RuO2 is nonmagnetic (muSR, neutron, ARPES); film signals are surface/interface or strain effects. In-window preprints on both sides: pro 2412.18220, 2602.15606; con/qualifying 2409.13504, 2508.15004, 2510.08064, 2511.00399, 2601.06791.
material: RuO2 (rutile), bulk crystals and epitaxial films
visibility_evidence: Smejkal et al. Science Advances 2020 (OpenAlex: 926 citations); Hiraishi et al. PRL 132, 166702 (163 citations); Kessler et al. npj Spintronics 2024 (122 citations); phys.org coverage Dec 2025.
notes: 2409.13504 is YYMM 2409 but its exact posting day relative to 2024-09-24 was not confirmed. 1901.00445 is the arXiv version of the Sci. Adv. 2020 paper (arXiv title 'Crystal Hall effect in Collinear Antiferromagnets').

name: Microsoft topological gap protocol / Majorana parity readout
claim: InAs-Al gate-defined nanowires pass the topological gap protocol (TGP) and host Majorana zero modes; interferometric single-shot parity readout and tetron X/Z loop measurements follow. Critique (Legg): TGP outcome depends on arbitrary data parameters and the readout regions are gapless/disordered. In-window: 2502.19560, 2503.08944 (comments), 2504.13240 (Microsoft response), 2507.08795 (tetron).
visibility_evidence: PRB 107, 245423 (OpenAlex: 216 citations); Nature 638, 651 (2025) with Microsoft 'Majorana 1' press launch; Legg's Matters Arising published in Nature 2026 with a Reply; coverage in Nature News, Science News, The Quantum Insider.
notes: 2504.13240 is a reply by the original authors (Aghaee et al.), listed under responses because it belongs to the Comment/Reply thread.

name: La3Ni2O7 pressurized superconductivity: bulk vs filamentary
claim: La3Ni2O7 single crystals superconduct near 80 K above ~14 GPa. Counter-claim: superconducting volume fraction ~1%, filamentary, possibly at La3Ni2O7/La4Ni3O10 intergrowth interfaces; later bulk SC shown in Pr-substituted La2PrNi2O7. In-window follow-on seen: 2510.13342 (La3-xSmxNi2O7 under pressure).
visibility_evidence: Sun et al. Nature 621, 493 (2023) (OpenAlex: 763 citations); Wang et al. Nature 634, 579 (2024) bulk SC (199 citations).
notes: Note 2311.12361 now carries the title 'Investigations of key issues on the reproducibility of high-Tc superconductivity emerging from compressed La3Ni2O7'.

name: Ambient-pressure superconductivity in strained La3Ni2O7 films
claim: Compressively strained (La,Pr)3Ni2O7 films on SrLaAlO4 superconduct at ambient pressure with onset 26-45 K; zero resistance only at ~2 K (Stanford) or BKT ~9 K (SUSTech), with mixed RP phases. Reproduced by at least two groups but bulk-ness/Tc spread still debated. In-window: 2412.16622, 2501.09255, 2603.02685, 2603.29531, 2608.17745.
material: La3Ni2O7 and La2.85Pr0.15Ni2O7 epitaxial thin films
visibility_evidence: Ko et al. Nature 638, 935 (2025) (OpenAlex: 200 citations; Author Correction 2026); Zhou et al. Nature 640, 641 (2025) (178 citations).
notes: The arXiv ID of Ko et al. (Stanford/SLAC) was NOT confirmed in this session and is intentionally omitted. Response IDs are follow-on studies (ARPES, pressure on films, reviews), not rebuttals.

name: Hg-1223 pressure-quench 151 K at ambient pressure
claim: A pressure-quench protocol (compress to ~30 GPa at low T, release) retains Tc up to 151 K in HgBa2Ca2Cu3O8+d at ambient pressure, a record ambient-pressure Tc; state is metastable (not stable to room temperature). Single-group result; no independent replication or rebuttal preprint found. In-window: 2603.12437.
visibility_evidence: PNAS 123, e2536178123 (March 2026); APS Physics Viewpoint/news (physics.aps.org/articles/v19/37); phys.org, Tom's Hardware, UH press release.

name: Room-temperature superconductivity in La-Sc-H (LaSc2H24)
claim: Laser-heated La-Sc alloy + ammonia borane at 250-260 GPa gives hexagonal LaSc2H24 with Tc onset 271-298 K (zero resistance, field suppression, 13 runs). Semenok/Troyan/Struzhkin et al. report 7 failed syntheses from La-Sc alloys at 250-280 GPa with no SC at 245-300 K. In-window: 2510.01273, 2601.01398, 2605.29985.
visibility_evidence: Physics World coverage ('Ternary hydride shows signs of room-temperature superconductivity'); also posted on Research Square (rs-7755852); theory prediction in PNAS 2024.
notes: Whether 2601.01398 is from the same group as 2510.01273 was not verified.

name: Hydride superconductivity evidence: flux trapping / Meissner (Hirsch-Marsiglio vs Eremets-Minkov)
claim: Trapped-flux SQUID measurements establish bulk superconductivity in H3S/LaH10 under pressure. Hirsch & Marsiglio argue the data are inconsistent with superconductivity; Comment ('Is MgB2 a superconductor?') and Reply exchange continues. In-window: 2412.05291 (Reply), 2501.01466.
material: H3S, LaH10 and other megabar superhydrides
visibility_evidence: The flux-trapping debate spans J. Supercond. Nov. Magn. and Physics of Metals and Metallography Comment/Reply (2025-2026).
notes: The Talantsev/Minkov/Eremets Comment appears on SSRN/Springer; its arXiv ID (if any) was not confirmed. SSRN was not accessed.

name: Time-reversal symmetry breaking / loop currents in kagome AV3Sb5
claim: The charge-density-wave state of AV3Sb5 breaks time-reversal symmetry (muSR, Kerr, STM, NMR loop currents). High-resolution Sagnac Kerr finds no spontaneous Kerr signal (<30 nrad). In-window: null 2510.26010; pro 2505.05150, 2605.05101, 2606.25251.
visibility_evidence: Mielke et al. Nature (2022) (OpenAlex: 521 citations); Saykin et al. PRL 131, 016901 (94 citations); Nature Physics 2026 'TRSB above the CDW order'.

name: UTe2 chiral (TRSB) superconductivity and pair-density wave
claim: UTe2 is a chiral, two-component TRSB spin-triplet superconductor (Kerr, split specific heat) hosting a pair-density wave (STM). Responses: no intrinsic Kerr signal, single-component SC (ultrasound), no bulk CDW (x-ray, elastic moduli), non-chiral order parameter; CDW/PDW possibly surface-only. In-window: 2501.16636, 2504.12505.
visibility_evidence: Hayes et al. Science (2021) (OpenAlex: 182 citations); Gu et al. Nature (2023) PDW (120 citations); Aishwarya et al. Nature 2023 (77); Theuss et al. Nature Physics 2024 single-component (50).
notes: The arXiv ID of Hayes et al. (Science 2021) was not confirmed in this session. Chiral/TRSB part leans refuted; PDW part contested (bulk vs surface).

name: Chiral superconductivity in rhombohedral graphene
claim: Rhombohedral tetra/pentalayer graphene hosts a chiral, TRSB superconductor emerging from a spin/valley-polarized metal (magnetic hysteresis in the SC state). Related SC + anomalous Hall reports from other groups (hexalayer, stripe order); direct thermodynamic/imaging confirmations appearing in 2026. In-window: 2504.05129, 2605.13303, 2606.05356, 2606.31851, 2608.12586, 2608.29873.
visibility_evidence: Han et al. Nature (2025) (OpenAlex: 120 citations within ~16 months).
notes: Group independence of the 2026 follow-ons was not checked; 2408.15233 (Aug 2024) precedes the window, publication (May 2025) is in-window.

name: Fractional quantum anomalous Hall effect in rhombohedral pentalayer graphene/hBN
claim: Zero-field FQAH plateaus at nu = 2/3, 3/5, ... in pentalayer graphene/hBN. Same group later finds that at lower electron temperature an extended integer QAH (EQAH) state replaces FQAH over a wide filling range; role of the moire potential disputed; an independent group reports FCIs in hexalayer graphene/hBN. In-window: 2609.09422, 2602.12737 (review).
material: Rhombohedral pentalayer/hexalayer graphene aligned to hBN
visibility_evidence: Lu et al. Nature 626, 759 (2024) (OpenAlex: 513 citations); EQAH Nature 2025 (99); Xie et al. Nature Materials 2025 (65).

name: Fractional quantum spin Hall effect in 2.1-degree twisted MoTe2
claim: Transport evidence for a fractional QSH insulator at nu = 3 (edge conductance 3/2 G0 per edge) in 2.1-degree tMoTe2. No independent experimental reproduction found; in-window activity is theory only (e.g. 2608.24989).
notes: 2608.24989 is a theory paper that does not cite/contest Kang et al. directly; listed only as in-window activity.

name: Half-quantized thermal Hall effect in alpha-RuCl3
claim: Half-integer quantized thermal Hall plateau (Majorana edge modes of a Kitaev spin liquid). Other groups see no quantization, strong sample dependence, oscillations from stacking faults, and phonon/magnon origins; phonon Hall viscosity (Nature 2026) accounts for a large fraction of kappa_xy. In-window: 2410.18342, 2510.06443.
visibility_evidence: Kasahara et al. Nature (2018) (OpenAlex: 897 citations); Czajka et al. Nature Physics 2021; phonon Hall viscosity paper in Nature 2026.
notes: 2005.00798 (sample dependence) is broadly supportive of quantization in best samples; listed with originals.

name: Excitonic insulator ground state of Ta2NiSe5
claim: Ta2NiSe5 is an intrinsic excitonic insulator below 326 K. Counter-claim: the symmetry breaking is primarily structural (phononic). In-window preprints on both sides: 2508.12363 (structural, UED), 2512.03011 (excitonic, STM), 2512.12439 (substrate tuning).
visibility_evidence: Lu et al. Nature Communications 8, 14408 (2017); Baldini et al. PNAS 120, e2221688120 (2023) (OpenAlex: 69 citations) with MPSD/EurekAlert press.
notes: No arXiv ID was found for the 2017 Lu et al. original; 2512.03011 is listed as the in-window pro-excitonic claim.
